channel.title: Market Pressure Map · Indian markets
channel.description: Daily news scored for its impact on Indian market sectors and the rupee, bonds, inflation and foreign flows.

item.title: Sensex falls 319 points to 81,592.45 and Nifty 0.61% to 25,144.30 on inflation and oil worries
item.description:
Autos, metals, realty and financials led Friday's selling after October inflation of 6.09% and a rebound in crude. Both indices still posted a third straight weekly gain. Rally pausing after Thursday's flat close.

Why it matters: Inflation above the RBI's ceiling raises rate-hike odds and hits rate-sensitive sectors first; costlier oil and higher US yields add pressure after a steep November rally.

Market gauges: Equities (Nifty & Sensex) −1, Inflation outlook −1

Confidence: high · horizon: days

item.title: Foreign investors buy a net ₹5,736.55 crore on Friday; domestic funds sell ₹2,253.58 crore
item.description:
Provisional exchange data show foreign buying continued despite the index fall, after ₹7,831 crore on Thursday. Ongoing: November inflows have been the strongest stretch in months.

Why it matters: Sustained foreign buying cushions equities and the rupee against higher US yields and oil, though domestic funds keep selling into the rally.

Market gauges: Foreign investor flows +2, Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +1, Rupee +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: Rupee falls 8 paise to 94.20 per dollar as the dollar index hits its highest since April 2025
item.description:
It opened at 94.07 and closed provisionally at 94.20, a second straight fall. Traders cited hot US inflation, rising Treasury yields, hawkish Fed remarks and weak equities. Reversing last week's gains.

Why it matters: A firmer dollar and costlier crude outweigh foreign equity inflows, raising imported inflation and hedging costs.

Market gauges: Rupee −1, Inflation outlook −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: days

item.title: 10-year G-Sec yield rises about 5 bps to 7.30% on higher US yields and supply worries
item.description:
The benchmark closed near 7.30–7.31% on Friday, up from 7.25%, on rising US Treasury yields and concern over extra bond supply. Escalating: up from 7.19% a week ago.

Why it matters: Higher sovereign yields lift borrowing costs for the government and companies and bring mark-to-market losses on banks' bond books.

Market gauges: Bond market (G-Secs) −2, Fiscal & trade balance −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: Economists see the repo rate at 6% by February after inflation breaches the RBI's band
item.description:
Most forecasters expect 25 bps in December and again in February from 5.50%; one large lender's research arm cut its December call to 25 bps from 50 and opposes a February hike. New after Thursday's 6.09% print.

Why it matters: A longer tightening path raises loan and deposit rates, slowing credit-led demand, though a smaller December move than feared limits the shock.

Market gauges: Bond market (G-Secs) −1, Growth outlook −1, Inflation outlook +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: months

item.title: October goods exports hit a record $49.47 billion, up 45%, but the goods deficit widens to $39.88 billion
item.description:
Imports rose to $89.35 billion; the goods gap is a one-year high and above the $32.25 billion forecast. Including services, the overall deficit narrowed to $20.09 billion from $25.15 billion a year earlier. New data.

Why it matters: Record exports support growth and manufacturing, but a wider goods gap driven by costly imports adds dollar demand and weighs on the rupee.

Market gauges: Growth outlook +2, Rupee −1, Fiscal & trade balance −1

Confidence: high · horizon: weeks

item.title: Forex reserves rise $2.49 billion to $719.55 billion in the week to 6 November
item.description:
Gold holdings rose about $2.2 billion to $104.8 billion; foreign currency assets edged up $232 million to $591.35 billion. Reverses the previous week's $2.69 billion fall.

Why it matters: A larger reserve buffer gives the RBI more room to smooth rupee swings as the dollar strengthens.

Market gauges: Rupee +1, Foreign investor flows +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: Brent holds near $96 but heads for a second weekly fall of about 2% as the US keeps its Iran blockade
item.description:
Brent traded around $95.5–96.5 on Friday with WTI near $88, after Thursday's 3.3% jump. Iran denied talks with Washington. Rebound from Tuesday's dip below $90 is holding.

Why it matters: Crude back in the mid-$90s keeps India's import bill, fuel under-recoveries and inflation risk high just as CPI has breached 6%.

Market gauges: Inflation outlook −1, Fiscal & trade balance −1, Rupee −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: Iran's Guards say two oil supertankers and an LNG tanker were disabled by mines in Hormuz
item.description:
Iran said the ships used an 'unauthorised' route; outbound Hormuz transits fell sharply and Iran ruled out nuclear inspections while under US threat. Escalating after record October attacks.

Why it matters: Mines add a new hazard on the route carrying much of India's crude and LNG, raising freight, insurance and supply risk as Gulf barrels overtake Russian supply.

Market gauges: Inflation outlook −1, Fiscal & trade balance −1, Growth outlook −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: US 10-year yield touches 5.17% and the dollar index 103.38 as markets price a December Fed hike
item.description:
The 2-year yield rose about 35 bps on the week, its biggest jump since September 2024, after Fed officials warned on inflation. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% on Friday. Escalating from Wednesday's hot CPI.

Why it matters: Higher US yields and a stronger dollar narrow India's yield advantage, threatening foreign inflows and pushing up the rupee's cost of defence and domestic yields.

Market gauges: Foreign investor flows −1, Rupee −1, Bond market (G-Secs) −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: Nasdaq falls 0.9% as chip and AI stocks slide after a leading chipmaker's chief resigns
item.description:
The Nasdaq-100 lost 1.22%, the weakest major US index on Friday, though the S&P 500 still gained 2.5% for the week. New.

Why it matters: A sell-off in US technology shares tends to spill into Indian IT stocks at Monday's open and can dent sentiment on AI-linked spending.

Market gauges: Equities (Nifty & Sensex) −1

Confidence: low · horizon: days

item.title: US assures India of tariffs below those on rival exporters as trade talks target a first-phase deal
item.description:
Reports say Washington promised India a tariff edge over peers; both sides aim to conclude a first phase by next month's G20 summit. Easing, despite this week's US duties on Indian solar panels.

Why it matters: A relative tariff advantage would help labour-intensive exporters win US orders; details and timing remain unconfirmed.

Market gauges: Growth outlook +1, Foreign investor flows +1, Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +1

Confidence: low · horizon: months
